title: Strain-Tuned Nodal Superconductivity in the Charge-Ordered Kagome Metal CsV$_3$Sb$_5$
authors: Yusuke Takeuchi, Akito Kobayashi, Saki Uchida, Takumi Nagao, Seigo Ogawa, Rui Zhou, Shinji Kawasaki, Fei Song, Hao Ni, Yong Zhao, Guo-qing Zheng
abstract: The nature of the superconducting pairing symmetry in the kagome metal CsV$_3$Sb$_5$ and its relationship with the charge density wave (CDW) order are central unresolved issues. Here, we investigate the evolution of superconductivity in CsV$_3$Sb$_5$ under in-situ uniaxial pressure using $^{121}$Sb nuclear quadrupole resonance (NQR). We find that tensile strain significantly enhances the superconducting transition temperature, $T_{\rm c}$, while the CDW remains unchanged, demonstrating that superconductivity can be tuned independently of the bulk charge order. At a tensile strain of $\varepsilon$ = +0.90%, the nuclear spin-lattice relaxation rate reveals a remarkable double transition: an upper transition at $T_{\rm c1}$ = 3.6 K to a nodal gap state, and a lower one at $T_{\rm c2}$ = 3.0 K characterized by a nodeless gap. These results evidence degenerate superconducting states with different gap symmetry in the kagome metal at ambient pressure which split under strain. Our work demonstrates a high tunability of superconductivity by uniaxial pressure.
summary: This work uses uniaxial strain on CsV3Sb5 to decouple and independently tune its superconducting state from its intrinsic Charge Density Wave (CDW) order. By analyzing NQR relaxation rates, the authors reveal a multi-gap superconductivity that is selectively enhanced by tensile strain through strengthening anisotropic pairing interactions. This demonstrates high tunability in correlated quantum materials.
main_problem: The study investigates the superconducting pairing symmetry in the charge-ordered Kagome metal CsV3Sb5 and how this superconductivity is tuned relative to the competing Charge Density Wave (CDW) order.
main_result: Tensile strain significantly enhances the superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$) by selectively strengthening the anisotropic d-wave pairing interaction, allowing for independent tuning of superconductivity away from the bulk CDW order.
method: The research employs in-situ uniaxial pressure tuning combined with advanced spectroscopic techniques like Nuclear Quadrupole Resonance (NQR) and measurements of the nuclear spin-lattice relaxation rate ($1/T_1T$).
model_or_system: The physical system is the Kagome metal CsV3Sb5, which exhibits both CDW order and unconventional superconductivity. The analysis models the superconducting state using a two-component (s+d) gap structure.
key_observables: Superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$), nuclear spin-lattice relaxation rate ($1/T_1T$) showing double transitions, and NQR spectral linewidth changes under strain.
important_parameters: Tensile strain ($\varepsilon = +0.90\%$), critical temperatures ($T_{c1} = 3.6 	ext{ K}$, $T_{c2} = 3.0 	ext{ K}$), and the ratio of d-wave to s-wave pairing strengths.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the superconducting state can be modeled as a weighted sum of anisotropic (d-wave) and isotropic (s-wave) components, and that strain primarily affects the pairing interaction strength rather than just the density of states.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate $T_c$ enhancement with strain; NQR spectra show domain detwinning ($	ext{Sb}(1)$ linewidth narrowing); and $1/T_1T$ measurements reveal a distinct double transition structure at high tensile strain, allowing for fitting to an s+d wave model.
paper_structure: The paper systematically addresses the competition between CDW and superconductivity using NQR under uniaxial strain. It first establishes that strain tunes $T_c$ independently of the robust CDW order. Subsequently, it uses detailed analysis of the temperature dependence of $1/T_1T$ to identify a multi-gap superconducting state whose enhancement is linked specifically to anisotropic pairing interactions.
why_interesting: The ability to tune superconductivity via strain while keeping the competing charge order intact provides a clean platform for studying unconventional pairing mechanisms, which is highly relevant to understanding correlated electron physics in quantum materials.

The solid curves represent the best fits using a sum of two Gaussian functions for the Sb(2) site and a single Lorentzian function for the Sb(1) site. Error bars represent the standard deviations from the fitting parameters.

FIG. 3. Temperature dependence of the 121Sb(2)-NQR 1/T1T under uniaxial strain. Data are shown for (a) ε = -0.46%, (b) 0, (c) +0.46%, (d) +0.68%, and (e) +0.90%. The 1/T1T and temperature (T) are normalized by their respective values at Tc(ε). The dashed lines mark the normalized transition point at T/Tc(ε) = 1, and the solid arrows indicate the onset of the superconducting transition. Error bars represent the standard deviations from the fitting parameters.
